## Appearance

Matthew Cuthbert is an odd-looking man with an ungainly figure, stooping shoulders, and kindly brown eyes. He has long iron-gray hair that reaches his shoulders and has worn a full, soft brown beard since he was twenty years old. Over the course of a year, his hair becomes noticeably grayer.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P34](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0034), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P26](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0026)_

## Personality

A notoriously quiet and shy man, Matthew is exceptionally uncomfortable around strangers and possesses a deep-seated dread of women, with the exception of [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. Rachel. He has a particular fear of little girls, believing women are often secretly laughing at him. Despite his hatred of being forced into conversation, he is a remarkably sympathetic, patient, and good-natured listener who enjoys the company of talkative people who do not expect him to speak. Characterized by his leniency and quiet wisdom, Matthew rarely scolds and excels at making excuses for others. When he forms an opinion or a desire, such as his disposition to keep [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), he displays an amazing, silent persistence that he holds to firmly without arguing.

## History

Matthew Cuthbert spent his youth at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), having grown up by the time the new house was built, and he wore a full brown beard after turning twenty. In his youth, he had once been lured onto a merry-go-round by another boy, and he grew to dread all women except for his sister [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md). Though he had not set foot upstairs in his own home for four years, he drove to [Bright River](../codex/places.md#bright-river) station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to find [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) waiting instead. Reluctant to confront the mistake, Matthew took her home to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and enjoyed her company along the drive. When [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) insisted on returning [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Matthew advocated for keeping her. He later secretly visited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in her room to persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Rachel after a dispute, enabling her to stay. He constantly supported [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), buying her chocolates and encouraging her involvement in events like the school flag concert. Intimidated by a female shop clerk while attempting to buy [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a fashionable dress, Matthew enlisted Mrs. Rachel's help to procure a puffed-sleeve dress for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) on Christmas morning. He proudly watched [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) excel in her studies, telling her he was prouder of her than of a dozen boys.

## Quotes

> "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P3](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0003)

> "It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman—dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P13](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0013)

> "That’s right—that’s right, Anne. But don’t tell Marilla I said anything about it. She might think I was putting my oar in and I promised not to do that."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P19](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0019)

> “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P25](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0025)

> “Well now, I guess you’ll manage all right,” said Matthew, looking at Anne’s white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes. “You just go right to bed and have a good sleep. I’ll do all the chores.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P38](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0038)
